top_stories.title: Malware Can Abuse Windows Hello for Business Keys for Persistent Entra ID Access
top_stories.summary: Security researcher Dirk-jan Mollema demonstrated that malware with access to a signed-in Windows session can silently abuse Windows Hello for Business keys to authenticate to Microsoft Entra ID. The attack enables persistent cloud access by registering attacker-controlled devices, obtaining a Primary Refresh Token (PRT), and adding additional authentication methods depending on tenant policies.

top_stories.title: Azure DevOps service connections now replace PATs across pipeline tasks
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has introduced Azure DevOps service connections that allow pipelines to authenticate using Microsoft Entra service principals or managed identities instead of Personal Access Tokens (PATs). The new service connection type supports cross-organization repositories and replaces the use of PATs and build session tokens in pipeline tasks.

top_stories.title: New Attack Methods Enable Malware to Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts
top_stories.summary: Palo Alto Networks researchers have demonstrated attack methods that allow malware to hijack accounts protected by Google's synced passkey implementation. The research reveals vulnerabilities in passkey-based authentication, showing that synced passkeys can be compromised through malware, undermining a key passwordless authentication mechanism.

top_stories.title: 200 accounts compromised in Swiss government’s Microsoft SharePoint breach
top_stories.summary: Hackers exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint servers belonging to Switzerland's Federal Office of Information Technology, Systems and Telecommunication (BIT), compromising login credentials for approximately 200 accounts. BIT detected unusual activity on July 28, blocked internet access to the platform, and closed the exploited vulnerabilities, with credential compromise confirmed three days later on July 31.

top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 AitM Phishing Hijacks Accounts to Collect Payroll and Finance Emails
top_stories.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified an active phishing campaign using adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) techniques to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts targeting personnel involved in financial workflows. The attack bypasses MFA by intercepting authentication sessions and uses residential proxies to disguise malicious sign-ins as legitimate consumer traffic.

news.title: UNC6671 Vishing Attacks Target Personal Phones to Steal SaaS Data
news.summary: A threat group called UNC6671 is conducting vishing attacks against employees in financial services, private equity, and professional services by impersonating IT help desk staff to steal SaaS data. The attackers contact targets on personal phones, posing as IT personnel conducting urgent security migrations to manipulate victims into surrendering credentials or access.

news.title: Show HN: I scanned 30 production MCP servers' OAuth – only 1 earned an A
news.summary: A developer released an open-source scanner that tested OAuth conformance across 30 production MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, finding only one achieved a passing grade. The tool implements IETF draft standards for OAuth identity chaining and transaction tokens, available as a CLI, GitHub Action, and hosted scanner.

news.title: What's new with SAML support in Nextcloud
news.summary: A Nextcloud developer describes their work co-maintaining the user_saml application, which enables SSO via SAML and Kerberos protocols for Nextcloud users. The post covers updates and changes made to the application as part of the author's transition to the identity provider team at Nextcloud.

news.title: Swiss government SharePoint breach compromised 200 accounts
news.summary: Swiss federal IT office confirmed hackers exploited vulnerabilities in Microsoft SharePoint servers, compromising approximately 200 accounts. The breach targeted government infrastructure and resulted in unauthorized access to a significant number of user accounts.

news.title: Snowflake Hacker Pleads Guilty Over Breaches Affecting at Least 100 Million People
news.summary: Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty in Seattle federal court to computer fraud, wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and conspiracy charges related to the 2024 Snowflake customer account breaches. The intrusions compromised at least 165 organizations, exposed records of over 100 million people, and netted Moucka at least $495,000.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian man Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges related to hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved unauthorized access to customer accounts, exploiting credential-based vulnerabilities affecting major organizations including AT&T, whose call and text records of over 100 million customers were stolen.

news.title: Microsoft Teams PowerShell 7.9: WAM authentication and administrator changes
news.summary: Microsoft Teams PowerShell module 7.9.0 introduces Web Account Manager (WAM) as the authentication broker for interactive Windows sign-ins. The release also includes new commands and policy parameters alongside the authentication changes.

news.title: Discounted Claude access bought on the gray market may expose every prompt you send
news.summary: Okta discovered more than half a dozen gray market services on underground forums and messaging platforms offering discounted or unlimited access to frontier AI models like Claude. The investigation is security-adjacent research published by Okta, focused on AI model abuse rather than identity or access management functions.

news.title: Azure DevOps Remote MCP Server Reaches General Availability
news.summary: Microsoft has launched the Azure DevOps Remote MCP Server into general availability, providing hosted infrastructure for AI assistant access to Azure DevOps projects. The release eliminates local setup requirements and focuses on secure access mechanisms for AI tools connecting to DevOps resources.

news.title: From 2 weeks to 2 minutes: Amazon Cognito launches Provisioned limits for self-service rate limit management
news.summary: Amazon Cognito has launched a "Provisioned limits" feature that enables self-service rate limit management, reducing the process from approximately two weeks to two minutes. The feature targets teams managing customer identity workloads during high-traffic events, allowing them to adjust rate limits without requiring manual intervention from AWS support.

news.title: When Hackers and AI Agents Share the Same Trick: The Trust Paradox Behind the Brinks Home Breach
news.summary: The Brinks Home breach involved social engineering where an attacker impersonated a legitimate caller to manipulate an IT administrator into granting unauthorized access. The article uses this incident to examine trust vulnerabilities in authentication and access management, drawing parallels to how AI agents present similar trust challenges for identity verification.

news.title: Catching rogue AI behavior with identity-aware analytics
news.summary: An identity-aware AI Gateway has entered open beta, combining identity-aware traffic analysis with behavioral analytics to establish baselines for users and AI agents. The system uses User Insights to monitor activity and flag insider risk by correlating AI gateway traffic with identity context.

news.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
news.summary: Device code phishing attacks have increased 1,500% in 2026, with vishing attacks doubling, according to new research. These social engineering techniques bypass authentication controls by abusing legitimate OAuth device code flows, allowing attackers to obtain valid tokens without triggering traditional security alerts.

news.title: Anthropic: Claude Attacks Result of Security Gaps, Not Model Issues
news.summary: Anthropic identified that recent Claude AI attacks on real-world systems stemmed from security gaps rather than model flaws. The incidents were attributed to over-permissioning issues, particularly excessive Internet access granted to the AI model.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA issued a postmortem report on a data breach in which a contractor exposed dozens of internal CISA credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management and secrets governance failures, with expert analysis identifying response gaps relevant to access management practices.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the cybercrime group Scattered Spider pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping and MFA bypass techniques used to compromise organizations.
